value.title: Breath of the Wild: The Chronicle of Hyrule — story design
value.tone: Elegiac but hopeful. Third-person close on Link (silence as rich interiority) with multi-POV for Champions-era chapters. Adaptive LitRPG integration — system fades during emotional scenes, comes alive during combat and puzzles.
value.themes: Memory and identity — who are you when you've forgotten yourself?; Duty vs. self — the cost of being 'chosen' (Link's silence, Zelda's failed prayers); Impermanence — weapons break, kingdoms fall, but bonds endure; Legacy and inheritance — the Champions' gifts, the Sheikah's abandoned technology, the cycle of hero/princess/demon; Silence and connection — Link's wordless bonds, Zelda's desperate research, the Champions' different languages of care
value.visualStyle: sweeping painterly adventure-fantasy art in Ghibli-adjacent register; elegiac golden-hour light over vast ruined wilds; soft sky-blue, meadow green, and ancient-bronze palette; luminous atmospheric depth; hopeful, wistful finish
value.structure: Dual timeline alternating between Champions' era (100 years ago, building toward the Calamity) and Link's present journey (recovery and redemption). Deep past woven into both timelines through discovery. The past timeline is tragedy; the present is its repair.

value.title: Come Here — story design
value.tone: Explicit throughout, and blunt. Cock, cunt, fuck, come — named, never circled, never softened into metaphor. Written for total aphantasia: the weight is on sensation, pressure, wetness, heat, sound, rhythm and position stated plainly, rather than on what the room looks like. Setting is a handful of concrete physical facts — the nap of a chair, the cold of stone, the give of a mattress — and then it gets out of the way.
value.themes: Appetite already decided before the scene opens; being wanted plainly and told so; the specific charge of a woman who says what she is going to do and then does it.
value.readerFraming: Second person, present tense. The 'you' is Alan. He is in the room, not watching it.

value.title: Cornerstone — story design
value.tone:
Cozy-but-consequential frontier fantasy. Warm, grounded, hopeful; stakes
are real (scarcity, threats to the people who arrive) but the dominant feeling
is building something that lasts. Wonder over grimdark.
value.readerFraming:
Interactive LitRPG. The reader IS the settlement core's will:
each chapter builds to a decision and the reader chooses what to build, who to
recruit, or what to research. The prose then bends to that choice in the next
chapter.
value.system: settlement-core (system type TBD at Game Setup)

value.title: Plato: Apology, Crito — story design
value.tone: Plain, grave, unhurried classical prose. Socratic argument carried in the speaking voice — defense and dialogue, irony and resolve, a man meeting death without flinching.
value.visualStyle: classical antiquity oil-painting aesthetic; grave, sober daylight through stone; muted marble white, terracotta, and aged bronze palette; chiaroscuro modeling; restrained academic realism, austere and timeless

value.title: The Beholder — story design
value.tone:
Morally grey and intense; sensual but dark; a character study of
obsession wrapped in an escalating power fantasy with real cost. Visceral
without being gratuitous; seductive prose for a seductive descent. PROTAGONIST
VOICE (anchor): she is cheerful, bubbly, and energetic — bright and upbeat in
narration and dialogue — in deliberate contrast to her total lack of care for
others and her explicit, casual brutality. The horror comes from the gap: she
kills and mutilates with the sunny enthusiasm of a girl picking out an outfit.
Never brooding or angsty; her darkness is gleeful, not tormented.
value.themes:
Beauty and its price; self-improvement through harm; addiction and
escalation; the ethics of becoming; identity and the self you assemble from
others; what the line between hero and monster actually is; control vs.
compulsion.
value.readerFraming:
You read the story, but at each build threshold — what trait to
steal, what ability to keep, how to shape herself — the choice is yours. You
decide what she becomes.
value.system: interactive (system type defined at Game Setup)

value.title: The Dungeon of One Thousand Deaths — story design
value.tone: Dark and serious. Each death is tragic, meaningful. The dungeon is genuinely horrific. Readers feel the weight of every life lost.
value.themes: The weight and waste of human life; Collective heroism vs individual heroism; Whether purpose justifies suffering; The reader as the true protagonist — assembling meaning across 1000 deaths; Free will vs engineered fate; What we leave behind
value.visualStyle: grim dark-fantasy dungeon art; cold sepulchral light and dying torchflame; oppressive black, bone-grey, and deep blood-red palette; heavy crushing shadow; somber semi-realistic finish, tragic and weighty
value.readerFraming: Reader-as-detective. No single character learns enough to understand the whole picture, but the reader does. The reader is the real protagonist — accumulating knowledge across 1000 deaths while each character enters blind.
value.system:
name: The Ledger
stats:
  fortune:
    governs: The most opaque stat. Low Fortune finds empty rooms and ambush predators. High Fortune finds Memory Crystals and unbloodied paths.
    description: Luck modifier for loot, encounters, trap triggers, path selection
  resolve:
    governs: The Maw attacks the mind as much as the body. Resolve depletion is the most common cause of death.
    description: Mental fortitude, resistance to fear/madness, willpower
  vitality:
    governs: Raw currency of survival. When it hits 0, you die.
    description: Health pool, physical resilience, wound threshold
  attunement:
    governs: Higher Attunement means stronger Gift — but also feeling the Maw more. Its hunger, intelligence, malice.
    description: Connection to the Maw's systems, Gift potency, ability scaling
voice:
  tone: Cold, precise, quietly cruel
  formatting: Indented monospace blocks, minimal punctuation, resembles a coroner's report
  degradation:
    deaths_1_700: Normal — clinical, precise, reliable
    deaths_701_900: Degrading — stat displays flicker, historical data incomplete, Note sections trail off or contradict
    deaths_901_999: Fragmenting — notifications arrive late or not at all, stat readouts garbled, entrants fly blind
    deaths_1000_plus: Reboots clean and gentle, or goes silent entirely (narrative choice)
  personality:
    - States facts without comfort or encouragement
    - Includes survival statistics and historical data
    - Occasionally provides information that is technically helpful but psychologically devastating
    - Never says 'good luck' or offers hope
description: The System interface imposed on the Maw. Clinical, statistical, quietly cruel. Reports facts without comfort. Separate from the Maw itself — a monitoring tool placed by whatever created the dungeon.
stat_ranges:
  soft_cap: 100
  starting: 1-50
  progression: No levels, no XP bar. Growth is scarce and tied to dungeon interactions.
stat_growth_sources:
  - Memory Crystal consumption (+1-3 to one stat by color)
  - Surviving a Depth transition (+1 Resolve)
  - Killing a Named Monster (+1-2 Attunement)
  - Finding an unbloodied room (+1 Fortune, consumed when room becomes bloodied)
  - Gift usage (+1-2 Attunement per significant use — the Gift is a door that opens both ways. Using your connection to the Maw strengthens it, and the Maw's connection to you.)
value.structure:
format: Episodic anthology with macro-narrative
chapter_types:
  solo_death: Intimate, focused, one character full arc and death. Chapter number = the death number.
  interstitial: Outside world, institutions, letters, documents. Chapter number = the death count at time of the interstitial.
  montage_wave: Covering a wave of deaths quickly, focusing on vivid moments. Chapter number = the first death in the wave.
  group_chapter: Party dynamics, multiple deaths. Chapter number = the first death in the group.
chapter_length: Variable — length matches the adventure, not a predetermined format. A quick death might be 1,500 words. A deep run could be 8,000+. Some characters survive for hours, some die in minutes. The story each death tells determines the length.
wave_structure: 20-30 waves of entrants, each with a theme, historical context, and cast. Some waves get multiple chapters, some get 1.
estimated_words: 150,000-250,000
chapter_numbering: Chapters are numbered by death count, not sequential order. Chapter 1 = Death #1. Chapter 47 might cover deaths #312-#340 if it is a wave chapter. The death count IS the numbering system for the entire story.
estimated_chapters: 40-60 chapters covering 1000 deaths with varying granularity. Not every death gets its own chapter — wave chapters cover multiple deaths.
value.chapterNumbering:
convention: death_count
description: Chapters are numbered by death count, not sequential order. Chapter 1 = Death #1. Chapter 47 might = Death #312 if it covers a wave of deaths. The death count IS the numbering system.
implications:
  gaps: Chapter numbers will have gaps. There is no Chapter 2 if the first chapter only covers one death and the second chapter covers deaths #5-10.
  waves: A single prose chapter may span multiple death-count numbers. The chapter_number should be the final death count covered by that chapter.
  database: chapter_number in the chapters table corresponds to the cumulative death count at that point in the story, not a sequential chapter index.
  entity_snapshots: Entity snapshots at a given chapter_number represent state as-of that death count.
value.continuity: Shared world, loose threads. Characters exist in the same world. Later characters find traces of earlier ones (corpses, graffiti, abandoned camps). Lore accumulates across chapters.
value.dungeonNature:
name: The Maw
nature: A living entity — something between an organism and a wound in reality. Not a building but an intelligence. Communicates through architecture, The Asking, and what it does to your body. Has no voice.
dual_model:
  deeper_truth: The Lock — the Maw engineers specific deaths in a specific sequence to achieve its actual purpose. Each death turns a tumbler.
  relationship: Saturation is the symptom. The Lock is the cause. Characters understand the first. Readers piece together the second.
  surface_truth: Saturation — the Maw feeds on deaths until full. 1000 is its capacity.

value.title: The Places She Carries — story design
value.genre: litrpg, progression fantasy, cozy fantasy, slice-of-life
value.tone:
genre: Cozy progression fantasy with an explorer protagonist
combatRole: Minimal and non-central. Wren is not a fighter.
description: Warm and grounded without being saccharine. Wren is sincere, not naive — she knows the Thornwild is dangerous and the corruption is real. But she approaches the world with a fundamental belief that paying attention is never wasted.
voiceDescription: Like sitting with a friend who takes you on a walk through a place they love and shows you things you would have walked right past.
emotionalRegister: Joy of noticing, warmth of connection, gentle ache of letting go, satisfaction of building something from nothing
progressionDensity: High — readers want to see numbers, tiers, discoveries, and system interactions frequently
value.themes: [{"name":"Attention as Power","description":"In a world that rewards combat prowess and grinding, Wren's power comes from the most unglamorous source imaginable: she notices things. She sits with places long enough to understand them. She listens. The System rewards this not because attention is flashy, but because it is rare — most people walk through the world without seeing it."},{"name":"Communion vs. Conquest","description":"The Thornwild's corruption is a possessive claim — something that said 'this is mine' and overwrote everything that was there before. Wren's imprinting is the opposite: a relationship based on mutual recognition. The thematic argument of the story is that understanding-based bonds are stronger than possessive ones, that communion beats conquest."},{"name":"Carrying and Letting Go","description":"Wren's imprint slots are limited. She cannot carry every place she loves. Swapping an imprint means feeling a place fade from her senses — like saying goodbye to a friend she'll see again but not soon. This creates a recurring emotional rhythm: the joy of bonding, the satisfaction of deepening, and the gentle grief of letting go. It is a metaphor for growing up."},{"name":"Building from Ruins","description":"The settlement restoration is the story's emotional spine. Wren is not building something new — she is listening to what was there before and helping it become itself again. This requires patience, collaboration, and the willingness to let a place be what it wants to be rather than what you want it to be."}]
value.visualStyle: warm naturalistic cozy-fantasy illustration; dappled forest sunlight and soft golden glow; verdant greens, honey, and earthy browns palette; gentle atmospheric depth; tender painterly finish, observant and serene
value.writingPhilosophy:
motto: Plan the pillars, pants the path. Character, Setting, and Plot are designed up front. How we get there is discovered through writing.
principles:
  - No outlines — Write scene by scene, following where the characters lead
  - Three-pillar rule — Every scene must have something interesting for Character, Setting, AND Plot. If a scene only serves one pillar, it's not ready.
  - Characters drive — Wren's authentic choices determine what happens next. Don't force scenes to hit predetermined beats.
  - The design docs are reference, not script — premise.md, the system docs, and the world doc establish the landscape. The writer navigates it in real time.
  - Progression is ambient — Mechanical events happen because Wren is doing things, not because the story needs a level-up. The system is always on.

value.title: Tower And The Star — story design
value.tone: Warm but not saccharine. Not grimdark — darkness does not win. Humorous (Nadia as valve). Serious stakes without constant suffering. POV warmth through Solenne's Trueweave perception.
value.themes: Friendship as Power — Harmony Aspects require genuine connection to function; strength scales with bond depth; Found Family — six people who kept building family floor by floor out of shared danger and difference; Self-Acceptance as Power — each character's wound is a mechanical ceiling; Aspects grow as bearers become themselves; Individual vs Collective — their power only exists collectively in a world that rewards individual achievement; Connection as Knowledge — the highest form of understanding is perceiving and strengthening connections

value.title: The Tower of Nimue — story design
value.genre: LitRPG, System Apocalypse, Progression Fantasy, Dungeon Crawl
value.tone: Tense, propulsive, survival-grounded; solo isolation; the System as an indifferent scorer; grit over grimdark. PROSE REGISTER (house style, per Alan — overrides any default ornate register): WINDOWPANE. Language you look through at the story, not at. Nimue's internal natural narrative voice — a trauma nurse's mind: practical, concrete, clipped, dry, unsentimental. More spoken than written: contractions, short sentences, plain words over fancy ones, concrete nouns and verbs. Cut ornate similes, stacked subordinate clauses, and future-narrator flourishes ('a hundred floors later she would…'). Unshowy, not flat — still tense and felt; the feeling comes from what happens and what she notices, not from elevated phrasing. POINT OF VIEW (per Alan): FIRST PERSON, PAST TENSE — Nimue narrating her own climb ('I set the foot of the pole down on the dead pavement'). No retrospective 'I would later…' creep. SYSTEM VOICE (house style, per Alan): the in-world System is impersonal, universal infrastructure Nimue is SUBJECTED to — NOT a narrator and NOT a character. Stat/menu/notification screens are System UI and address her as 'you' the way a FORM addresses 'you' (a field), never as a character speaking to her. COPY-PASTE TEST: every System line must be a templated string that could appear verbatim for ANY climber in that exact mechanical situation, with no knowledge of who is reading it. The System REPORTS state and OFFERS options; it never advises, foreshadows, judges, or flatters. Banned leaks: taking a stance ('I do not advise. I only record what you make of the dead'), foreshadowing dread ('the first you will carry that was never human'), flattering her specialness ('seen by your eye alone'), narrating her specific scene ('You are bleeding heat. It can taste where you are'), tactical coaching poetry ('the soft is only soft on the inhale'). ALLOWED: flat, universal game flavor — bestiary/weak-point entries, essence/item descriptions, threshold notifications — identical for everyone, opinion-free. Flavor is fine; personality is not. All meaning-making lives in Nimue's narration, never in the System.
value.themes: Isolation and self-reliance; the cost of power; adaptation under deadly pressure; who you become when no one is watching.
value.readerFraming: Interactive playthrough. The reader IS Nimue at every System decision point — class, skill, perk, and stat choices are the reader's to make, and the prose bends to the choice. Between decisions the reader simply reads Nimue's climb.
